results.title: DigitalOcean GPU Droplets: cards, regions, billing - AI Hosting Index
results.author: George D
highlights:
Last updated 6 November 2026 · . By George

DigitalOcean rents whole GPU servers, called GPU Droplets, with NVIDIA H100, H200, L40S, RTX 4000 Ada and RTX 6000 Ada cards and AMD MI300X cards. It bills by the second, with 60 seconds at least, and the bill runs until you destroy the Droplet.

Each price covers the whole machine: the GPU, processor cores, memory and disks. This guide lists the plans and regions from DigitalOcean's own documentation, read on 6 November 2026, with prices from our weekly price records.

A GPU Droplet is a whole server around one or eight cards like these, billed by the second. Photo: Nana Dua, Pexels.

## How the bill works

- By the second: billing starts when you create the Droplet and stops when you destroy it, with 60 seconds at least.
- Powered off is still billed: the GPU stays reserved for you, so switching the Droplet off does not stop the charge.
- No monthly ceiling: the 672-hour monthly cap of DigitalOcean's ordinary Droplets does not apply to GPU Droplets.
- Spot machines: in public preview, at a daily price never above on-demand. DigitalOcean gives at least 2 hours' notice before it takes one back.
- Data transfer: incoming traffic and traffic inside your private network are free. Outgoing traffic above your team's pooled allowance is billed by the gigabyte.

New accounts may be charged partway through the month when they create GPU Droplets. DigitalOcean says the total does not change.

...

## How we checked

We read DigitalOcean's Droplet features page, its GPU availability page and its Droplet pricing documentation on 6 November 2026. DigitalOcean last verified the availability page on 10 August 2026.

...

### Does DigitalOcean have spot GPUs?

Yes, in public preview. The price changes daily but never goes above on-demand, and DigitalOcean gives at least 2 hours' notice before taking one back.

results.title: What are the best DigitalOcean GPU Droplet alternatives? | Nodus Blog
results.author: Nodus Compute Engineering
highlights:
The best DigitalOcean GPU Droplet alternatives are Nodus for training and fine-tuning that must survive a lost machine, RunPod for cheap hourly pods, and Lambda for big NVIDIA machines and reserved clusters. Nodus lists the NVIDIA H100 at $2.60/hr against DigitalOcean’s $4.41 on-demand rate, restores your latest checkpoint on a replacement machine, and can run jobs in your own DigitalOcean account first (Beta). Stay on DigitalOcean if you want AMD Instinct GPUs, a 12-month reserved price, or a plain virtual machine next to the rest of your DigitalOcean setup.

CPU Droplets start at $4 per month and have billed per second since January 1, 2026, with a 60-second minimum or $0.01, whichever is higher. ## How Droplet pricing and monthly caps work

Effective January 1, 2026, DigitalOcean moved to per-second billing for Droplets, with a minimum charge of 60 seconds or $0.01, whichever is higher. If you spin up a server via a script and tear it down 15 seconds later, you still pay for the full minute or the penny minimum.

results.title: DigitalOcean price increase 2022: the $5 Droplet became $6
results.author: Fieldnote Labs
highlights:
One email a month with the price changes we confirm on the 355 pricing pages we read.

...

DigitalOcean raised prices on July 1, 2022. It was the first price change in the company's history. The classic $5 Basic Droplet went to $6 a month, a 20% increase, and most Basic Droplets went up by the same 20%. DigitalOcean added a new $4 Droplet with 512MB of memory as the new entry point. Snapshots, Load Balancers, Reserved IPs, and Custom Images went up on the same day. Live plan data is on the DigitalOcean pricing page on SaaS Price Watch.

## Old and new prices

Basic Droplets (regular CPU), per month. Old prices are from the Droplet pricing page in May 2022. New prices are from the same page in August 2022.

| Basic Droplet | Old price | New price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 512MB, 1 vCPU | not offered | $4 a month | new plan |
| 1GB, 1 vCPU | $5 a month | $6 a month | +$1, 20% |
| 2GB, 1 vCPU | $10 a month | $12 a month | +$2, 20% |
| 2GB, 2 vCPUs | $15 a month | $18 a month | +$3, 20% |
| 4GB, 2 vCPUs | $20 a month | $24 a month | +$4, 20% |
| 8GB, 4 vCPUs | $40 a month | $48 a month | +$8, 20% |
| 16GB, 8 vCPUs | $80 a month | $96 a month | +$16, 20% |

General Purpose Droplets rose by a smaller step. The 8GB General Purpose Droplet went from $60 to $63 a month, a 5% increase.

...

## What DigitalOcean said

The May 16, 2022 blog post says: "for the first time there will be a price change on some of our products from July 1, 2022, combined with the introduction of a new, more affordable $4 Droplet."

The July 1, 2022 release notes say the prices of Droplets, Snapshots, Load Balancers, Reserved IPs, and Custom Images increased. The same note lists no change to Spaces, backups, volumes, the Container Registry, or App Platform.

## Who it hits and when

- All Droplet customers, new and existing, from July 1, 2022.
- Snapshots, Load Balancers, Reserved IPs, and Custom Images went up on the same date.
- Spaces, volumes, backups, the Container Registry, and App Platform had no change in this round.
- We do not list the Managed Database and Kubernetes changes here. We could not match old and new prices to a source we can cite.

## What to do before your renewal

DigitalOcean bills by usage, so there is no renewal date. The new prices apply to the next bill.

...

## FAQ

When did DigitalOcean raise prices? On July 1, 2022. DigitalOcean announced the change on May 16, 2022.

How much did the DigitalOcean $5 Droplet go up? It went from $5 to $6 a month, a 20% increase. The specs (1GB memory, 1 vCPU) stayed the same.

Can I buy a $5 DigitalOcean Droplet today? No. The cheapest Basic Droplet after the change is $4 a month with 512MB of memory. The 1GB Droplet costs $6 a month.

Did existing DigitalOcean customers pay the new price? Yes. The change applied to all customers from July 1, 2022. The release notes say the new prices were in effect from that date.

...

## Why the deal price is different

A list price is for one GPU, today, with no commitment. A large deal changes every one of those terms.

- Term. A commitment of one year or more is priced below on-demand. DigitalOcean, for example, publishes $3.26 a GPU-hour for an H100 on a 12-month reservation.
- Volume. A cluster of thousands of GPUs is a different product from a single instance. The seller fills a whole hall at once.
- Payment. A deposit or prepayment buys a lower rate. It also moves risk from the seller to the buyer.
- Start date and place. Capacity that is live today costs more than capacity that goes live next year. A region with spare power costs less than one without.
- What is in the hour. Fast networking between GPUs, storage, support and data transfer are priced in some quotes and added on in others.

### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

results.title: What Is DigitalOcean? Inside the AI-Native Cloud (2027)
results.author: Jesse Sumrak Sr. Content Marketing Manager
highlights:
### Infrastructure

GPU Droplets and Bare Metal GPUs provide NVIDIA and AMD accelerators for training, fine-tuning, and dedicated inference (billed per second on demand).

DigitalOcean owns the GPUs it runs, rather than reselling third-party capacity, so GPU pricing is not subject to a reseller markup. Actual costs vary by configuration, region, and workload.

The infrastructure layer includes:

- 20 data centers across 13 regions, with air-cooled and liquid-cooled infrastructure
- NVIDIA H100, H200, and HGX B300 GPUs
- AMD Instinct MI300X, MI325X, MI350X, and MI355X GPUs
- 400G RoCE fabric for high-bandwidth, low-latency GPU-to-GPU networking

...

DigitalOcean keeps pricing simple and transparent with an all-in-one bill. Rates below are in USD, exclude applicable taxes, and are subject to change; Public Preview pricing may change at general availability. See the pricing page for current rates:

- Serverless inference: From about $0.05 per million tokens, depending on the model.
- Dedicated inference: From $2.59 per GPU-hour (AMD Instinct MI300X), depending on GPU type and configuration.
- Batch inference: Up to 50% off real-time rates on supported OpenAI and Anthropic models.
- Harness Runtime: $0.044 per vCPU-hour and $0.0095 per GB-hour, billed per second. An idle agent’s CPU charge drops to zero.
- Action Gateway: $0.10 per 1,000 standard tool calls, with tool search included.
- App Platform: From $5 per month for a container, with a free tier for static sites.
- Managed Databases: PostgreSQL from $15.15 per month.
- Inference Router: No separate routing fee. You pay only for the model that serves each request.
